b. Per capita income (Gadgil-Mukherjee) | ii. 10%
c. Tax effort (Gadgil-Mukherjee) | iii. 25%
d. Per capita income (Gadgil, 1969) | iv. 7.5%
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
100.x: Population 60% in both; per capita income 25% in Gadgil-Mukherjee (10% in Gadgil); tax effort 7.5% in Gadgil-Mukherjee (10% in Gadgil).

100.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gadgil formula:
1. It was endorsed by the National Development Council in 1968-69 and used from the Fourth Plan (1969).
2. Irrigation and power projects were a criterion in the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula but not in the original Gadgil formula.
3. The first Special Category States – Assam, J&K and Nagaland – received assistance as 90% grant and 10% loan.
How many of the above statements are correct?
100.x: Two are correct (1 and 3). Statement 2 is reversed: irrigation and power projects (10%) were in the Gadgil formula (1969) and dropped in Gadgil-Mukherjee (1991). General States got 30% grant, 70% loan.

100.s: After the loss of the revenue deficit grant, what is Andhra Pradesh's revenue deficit in Budget 2026-27?
100.x: With the 16th FC ending revenue deficit grants, AP's revenue deficit is 1.1% in Budget 2026-27.

100.s:
Match List-I (Central transfer to Andhra Pradesh) with List-II (Amount):
List-I | List-II
a. 16th FC – rural local bodies | i. ₹62,188 crore
b. 16th FC – urban local bodies | ii. ₹12,158 crore
c. 16th FC – disaster grant | iii. ₹16,627 crore
d. All FC grants, 2025-26 (RE) | iv. ₹6,125 crore
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
100.x: 16th FC to AP: rural local bodies ₹16,627 crore, urban ₹12,158 crore, disaster ₹6,125 crore; FC grants (₹62,188 crore of ₹1,04,493 crore in 2025-26 RE) are AP's largest central transfer.

101.s: How much percentage of the Grants-in-Aid to Panchayats is recommended by 14th Finance Commission as Basic grant?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
101.x: The 14th Finance Commission split grants to gram panchayats 90% basic grant and 10% performance grant (urban bodies 80:20).

101.s: The Twelfth Finance Commission followed data of which Census for assigning weights to population while recommending grants to local bodies?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
101.x: For local-body grants the 12th FC gave population a 40% weight using Census 2001 data (it used 1971 population only for tax devolution).

101.s: Which Finance Commission used the same amount of Per capita grant assistance as the basis both for the Rural and Urban Local Bodies for awarding Grants-in-aid for local bodies is
101.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
101.x: The 14th FC split its local-body grants between rural and urban areas by population (2011), so the same per capita amount (about ₹488 per head a year on aggregate) applied to both.

101.s: The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended that States may permit levy of the following tax by Panchayats?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
101.x: The 14th FC asked States to empower local bodies to levy advertisement tax (para 9.93) and to improve local revenues; sales tax and excise are State/Union taxes.

101.s: The recommendations of Central Finance Commission on grants to local bodies are?
o: Partly based on reports of SFCs
Entirely based on reports of SFCs
Not based on reports of SFCs
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
101.x: In practice the Union FCs have not based local-body grants on SFC reports (SFC reports are irregular and out of step); they use their own criteria such as population and area (APPSC key).

101.s: As recommended by the fourteenth finance commission, the performance grant of a panchayat for one year would be released?
o: In the last quarter of the same year based on utilization certificates
In the last quarter of the same year based on audit report for 3 quarters
Would be released in the next year based on audited accounts of the year
Would be released in the last year of the five year period based on audited accounts of four years
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
101.x: Under the 14th FC, performance grants to gram panchayats ran from 2016-17 and were released in a later year against audited annual accounts (not older than two years) and a rise in own revenue – so "next year, based on audited accounts".

101.s: What is the amount of grant-in-aid recommended by the 14th Finance Commission to the Panchayats during 2015 – 2020?
101.x: The 14th FC recommended ₹2,87,436 crore for local bodies for 2015-20, of which ₹2,00,292.2 crore for gram panchayats and ₹87,143.8 crore for municipalities.

101.s: As per the recommendations of the 14th Finance Commission, out of the grant-in-aid what would be the proportion of basic grant and performance grant in the case of Municipalities?
101.src: Technical Assistant (Geo Physics), Technical Assistants in A
101.x: 14th FC: basic:performance grant was 90:10 for gram panchayats and 80:20 for municipalities.

101.s: United grants are also known as general purpose or block grants because
101.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
101.at: They can be used by the Panchayat Raj Institutions (PRIs) according to their needs and priorities, with no conditions attach to their utilization
101.x: Untied (basic/general-purpose) grants carry no conditions – PRIs spend them on their own needs and priorities, unlike tied grants.

101.s: The Eleventh Finance Commission gave the following weightage to population as per 1991 Census while recommending grants to local bodies?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
101.x: The Eleventh Finance Commission gave population (1991 Census) a 40% weight in grants to local bodies; the other weights were area 10%, distance from highest per capita income 20%, decentralisation index 20% and revenue effort 10%.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the 15th Finance Commission's rural local body grants:
1. Provisional and audited accounts must be in the public domain for at least 25% of rural local bodies.
2. Constitution of the State Finance Commission is mandatory for release from 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: Both are release conditions: accounts in the public domain for at least 25% of rural local bodies, and an SFC from 2024-25.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about entry conditions for local bodies under the 16th Finance Commission:
1. Audited accounts must be published online.
2. Issue of municipal bonds is mandatory.
3. The State Finance Commission must be constituted on time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: The entry conditions are elected bodies, online audited accounts and timely SFCs; issuing municipal bonds is not a condition.

101.s:
Match List-I (Finance Commission) with List-II (Grants recommended for local bodies):
List-I | List-II
a. 10th | i. ₹87,519 crore
b. 13th | ii. ₹7,91,493 crore
c. 15th | iii. ₹4,36,361 crore
d. 16th | iv. ₹4,380 crore for PRIs + ₹1,000 crore for ULBs
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
101.x: 10th FC – ₹4,380 crore PRIs + ₹1,000 crore ULBs (first, ad hoc local-body grants); 13th – ₹87,519 crore; 15th – ₹4,36,361 crore (rural ₹2,36,805 crore); 16th – ₹7,91,493 crore.

101.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The 14th Finance Commission gave its rural local-body grants only to gram panchayats, not to the block and district tiers.
Reason (R): The 14th Finance Commission fixed the basic-to-performance grant ratio at 90:10 for gram panchayats.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
101.x: Both are true (14th FC: gram panchayats only; 90:10 for gram panchayats, 80:20 for municipalities), but the grant ratio does not explain why the other tiers were left out.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the 15th Finance Commission's local-body grants:
1. 60% of the rural grants are tied (drinking water, sanitation) and 40% untied.
2. The untied part may be used to pay salaries.
3. Urban local bodies must notify floor (baseline) property-tax rates to get the grants.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
101.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 40% untied grant cannot be used for salaries.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission's local-body grants:
1. The basic grant is 80% of the total, half tied (water, sanitation) and half untied.
2. The performance grant is 20% and fully tied.
3. The urban share of local-body grants rises from 36% to 45%.
4. Issue of municipal bonds is an entry condition for the grants.
How many of the above statements are correct?
101.x: Two are correct (1 and 3). Statement 2 is wrong: the performance grant is fully untied. Statement 4 is wrong: the entry conditions are elected bodies, audited accounts online and timely SFCs – municipal bonds are not a condition.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission's urban grants:
1. The Urbanisation Premium is a one-time grant of ₹10,000 crore.
2. It is linked to merging peri-urban villages under a Rural-to-Urban Transition Policy.
3. The special infrastructure grant of ₹56,100 crore is for wastewater in cities with population above 40 lakh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the ₹56,100 crore wastewater grant is for cities of 10-40 lakh population.

101.s: In matching grant, what percentage of grants is to be arranged by Panchayat as a matching share?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
101.x: Under the matching-grant pattern a panchayat had to raise about 10% of the grant amount as its own matching share (APPSC key).

101.s: With regard to Backward region grant fund (BRGF), after receipt of funds from Centre, the state government has to release the funds within how many days to Panchayat Raj Institutions?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
101.x: BRGF guidelines required States to release the Central funds to Panchayati Raj Institutions within 15 days of receipt.

101.s:
Which of the following source/sources of revenue qualifies/qualify for being given to the Panchayats?
I. The tax proceeds that are assigned to the States from the Centre may be again re-distributed to the Panchayats as recommended by the Central Finance Commission.
II. Loans from the State Government.
III. Under Article 243-I of the Constitution of India. the State Government is empowered to devolve its own funds to the Panchayats even in the absence of the State Finance Commission's recommendations.
IV. Internal Resource Generation is facilitated only in the case of Panchayats situated in Scheduled Areas as per the Fifth Schedule.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
101.x: Only II is right: panchayats may take loans from the State. I is wrong (sharing with panchayats is on SFC, not Central FC, advice), III is wrong (Art. 243-I creates the SFC; devolution under Art. 243H), IV is wrong (own resources are not limited to Fifth Schedule areas).

101.s: Out of the following, which is the major source of revenue for Panchayats?
101.src: APPSC 2018 Special Qualifying Test for Appointment by Promot
101.x: Property tax (house tax) is the major own revenue source of panchayats.

101.s: Which of the following taxes is levied by the Gram Panchayats?
101.x: Gram panchayats may levy only State-authorised taxes such as tax on local fairs, house tax, fees and tolls; sales tax and land revenue are State levies.

101.s:
Consider the following sources of Revenue of the Panchyats :
1. Local Authority Grant by Finance Commission
2. Assistance by Central Cooperative Banks
3. Allocations for Centrally Sponsored Schemes
4. NABARD
5. Allocation from State Finance Commission Of the above, the correct sources of Finance for Panchyats would be?
101.x: Panchayat finance comes from Finance Commission local-body grants, central cooperative bank assistance, CSS allocations and SFC devolution; NABARD refinances banks and does not fund panchayats directly.

101.s: Own revenue as percentage of assigned revenue in case of Panchayat Raj Institutions in Andhra Pradesh during 2014-15 is nearly?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
101.x: Printed key kept: own revenue of AP's PRIs was about 27% of assigned revenue in 2014-15 (AP SFC data); not verified.

101.s: Being constrained in their power to tax, on which of the following do panchayats substantially depend?
101.x: Panchayats depend substantially on grants; gram sabhas spend only about 4% of their time on revenue generation.
xa: Panchayat sources: **FC local body grants**, **Central Cooperative Banks**, **CSS**, **SFC** allocations.
⚠ **NABARD** is not a direct source.
**SVAMITVA** drone maps provide a panchayat **property-tax baseline**.

101.s: Under which Constitutional Act, provisions were made for allocation of grants to Panchayats from the Central government on the recommendations of Central Finance Commission?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
101.x: Clause (bb) of Art. 280(3) – the Central FC recommending measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund for panchayats – was added by the 73rd Amendment (1992); the 80th Amendment (2000) only changed tax sharing (Art. 270).

101.s: In terms of procedures for determination of grants, State Finance Commissions have to follow?
o: Procedure laid down by State Government
Procedure laid down by Central Finance Commission
Procedure laid down in the Panchayat Raj Acts
They can design their own procedures
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
101.x: Like the Union FC, a State Finance Commission determines its own procedure (State PR Acts, on the Art. 243-I model).

101.s: Which of the following statements about State Finance Commission is / are correct? i. This Commission examines the financial position of the governments in the State. ii. It also review the distribution of revenues between the State and Local governments on the one hand and between rural and urban local governments on the other.
101.x: The SFC reviews the financial position of panchayats and municipalities and recommends the distribution of State revenues between the State and local bodies, and among the local bodies (rural and urban).

101.s: Devolution of taxing and spending powers to lower levels of government is known as ____
101.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
101.x: Devolving taxing and spending powers to lower levels of government is fiscal decentralisation. (Moved: fiscal decentralisation to local bodies, row 101.)

101.s:
Consider the following statements about State Finance Commissions:
1. There is no separate State Finance Commission for Municipalities.
2. The State Finance Commission constituted under Article 243I also reviews municipal finances under Article 243Y.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: Both are correct: the same SFC constituted by the Governor under Article 243I reviews municipal finances under Article 243Y, so no separate SFC exists.

101.s: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution?
101.x: The Eleventh Schedule (Art. 243G) lists 29 subjects; the Twelfth (Art. 243W) lists 18.

101.s: In the decentralisation debate, what do the '3Fs' that rarely move together to local bodies refer to?
101.x: The Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules are only enabling, so funds, functions and functionaries rarely move together.

101.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Under Article 243H, a State Legislature is not compelled to authorise panchayats to impose taxes.
Reason (R): Article 243H uses the word 'may', making it an enabling provision.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
101.x: Both are true and R explains A: 'may' makes Art. 243H enabling – the Legislature may authorise taxes, tolls and fees, assign State taxes and give grants, but is not forced to.

101.s:
Match List-I (Article) with List-II (Provision):
List-I | List-II
a. 243H | i. Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission every five years
b. 243-I | ii. The same SFC reviews the finances of municipalities
c. 243Y | iii. Twelfth Schedule – 18 subjects for municipalities
d. 243W | iv. State Legislature may authorise panchayats to levy taxes, tolls and fees
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
101.x: 243H – enabling taxation power for panchayats; 243-I – Governor constitutes an SFC every five years; 243Y – the same SFC reviews municipal finances (no separate SFC); 243W – Twelfth Schedule, 18 subjects (243G – Eleventh Schedule, 29).

101.s: Who is the Chairman of the Fourth Finance Commission constituted by the Government of Andhra Pradesh?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
101.x: AP constituted its Fourth State Finance Commission on 5 Jan 2015 under Prof. M.L. Kantha Rao (the 2017 exam answer); it was wound up in March 2017 and reconstituted on 8 Feb 2018 under Prof. G. Nancharaiah, who submitted the report on 30 Oct 2019.

101.s: The Second Finance Commission of AP was set up in?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
101.x: AP's Second State Finance Commission was constituted on 8 Dec 1998 under Prof. D.L. Narayana (award 2000-05); the First SFC was set up in June 1994.

101.s: The First State Finance Commission of AP recommended the following portion of tax and non-tax revenues to be devolved to Local Bodies?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
101.x: AP's First SFC (T. Laxmana Swamy, report May 1997) recommended devolution that worked out to 39.24% of the State's own tax and non-tax revenue.

101.s: The First State Finance Commission of AP recommended that Panchayats may be categorized into various categories based on?
101.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
101.x: AP's First SFC distributed funds among gram panchayats by their stage of development – ordinary, advanced, backward and tribal.

101.s: Which period does the report of Andhra Pradesh's Fifth State Finance Commission (31 Dec 2024) cover?
101.x: The 5th SFC reported on 31 Dec 2024 for 2025-30.

Consider the following statements about State Finance Commissions in Andhra Pradesh:

2. Its members are appointed by the Chief Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: AP's SFC has a chairman and 4 members, but they are appointed by the Governor, not the Chief Minister.

101.s:
Match List-I (Andhra Pradesh State Finance Commission) with List-II (Chairman):
List-I | List-II
a. First (1994) | i. T. Laxmana Swamy
b. Second (1998) | ii. Prof. S. Rathna Kumari
c. Fourth (reconstituted 2018) | iii. Prof. D.L. Narayana
d. Fifth | iv. Prof. G. Nancharaiah
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
101.x: 1st AP SFC (22 June 1994) – T. Laxmana Swamy; 2nd (8 Dec 1998) – Prof. D.L. Narayana; 4th – Prof. M.L. Kantha Rao (2015), reconstituted 8 Feb 2018 under Prof. G. Nancharaiah; 5th – Prof. S. Rathna Kumari (report 31 Dec 2024, for 2025-30).

101.s: Payment on municipal water supply is called
101.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M

101.s: Which of the following tax is not collected by Central Govt.?
101.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economics & Statistical Servi
101.x: Property tax is levied by local bodies (State List entry 49 assigned to them); customs, corporation tax and income-tax surcharge are Central taxes.

101.s:

2. Professional tax is subject to a ceiling of ₹2,500.
3. Rents and user charges such as payments for municipal water supply are tax revenue.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: rents, fees, fines and user charges (water supply, sewerage) are non-tax revenue.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about property tax:
1. Under-assessment and under-collection of property tax mainly explain weak municipal finances.
2. The Economic Survey 2016-17 used satellite imagery to estimate the property-tax gap in Bengaluru and Jaipur.
3. SVAMITVA drone maps can give panchayats a property-tax baseline.
4. The Smart Cities Mission rewards cities for property-tax reform and municipal bonds.
How many of the above statements are correct?
101.x: Three are correct (1, 2, 3). Statement 4 is wrong: it is AMRUT 2.0 that rewards property-tax reform and municipal bonds.

101.s: Which committee recommended that the "Panchayats should have special powers to levy special tax on land revenues and home taxes"
101.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
101.x: The K. Santhanam Committee on Panchayati Raj Finances (1963) said panchayats should have special powers to levy taxes on land revenue and house tax.

o: Local Finance Enquiry Committee (1949-51) – P.K. Wattal
Committee on Panchayati Raj Finances (1963) – John Matthai
101.x: The Local Finance Enquiry Committee (1949-51) was headed by P.K. Wattal. John Matthai chaired the Taxation Enquiry Commission, K. Santhanam the Committee on Panchayati Raj Finances and A.P. Jain the Rural-Urban Relationship Committee.

101.s:

101.x: Two are correct (1 and 3). Statement 2 is wrong: India's transfers to local bodies are only about 0.5% of GDP; 2-5% is the global norm.

101.s: About how much is the 16th Finance Commission's grant to Andhra Pradesh's urban local bodies?
101.x: AP's urban LBs get ₹12,158 crore and rural LBs ₹16,627 crore under the 16th FC.

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

102.s:
The reasons for fast growth of public expenditure in India in recent years are

A. Urbanisation
B. Interest payments

C. Subsidies
D. Defense expenditure
102.x: Urbanisation, rising interest payments, subsidies and defence all pushed up public expenditure – "all of these".

102.s: According to Economic Survey 2016-17, the ratio of public expenditure to GDP stands at approximately?
o: None of the given answers are correct
102.x: Economic Survey 2016-17 put combined Centre and State spending at about 28% of GDP.

102.s: In the Union Budgets in India, which one of the following is the largest in amount?
102.x: Revenue expenditure (about three-fourths or more of Union spending) is the largest; it was larger than non-plan, plan or capital expenditure.

102.s: Which is the largest item under Non-Plan Expenditure of Central Government?
102.x: Interest payments were the single largest item of non-plan expenditure, ahead of defence, subsidies and pensions.

102.s: In the Union Budget the largest item of revenue expenditure is :
102.x: Interest payments are the largest item of Union revenue expenditure (BE 2026-27: about 26% of total spending and 40% of revenue receipts), ahead of defence, subsidies, grants and pensions.

102.s: Which one of the following is not true about the total outlay in the Union Budget 2023-24?
o: State share of taxes and duties (18%)

102.s: The largest item of public expenditure in the Union Budgets in recent years is :
102.x: Interest payments are the largest item of Union revenue expenditure (BE 2026-27: about 26% of total spending and 40% of revenue receipts), ahead of defence, subsidies, grants and pensions.

102.s: Which among the following is the largest item of current revenue expenditure of Central Government in the year 2008-10?
o: Grants to States and Union Territories
102.x: Interest payments are the largest item of Union revenue expenditure (BE 2026-27: about 26% of total spending and 40% of revenue receipts), ahead of defence, subsidies, grants and pensions.

102.s: Which among the following is the most important item of revenue expenditure of the Union Government?
102.x: Interest payments are the largest item of Union revenue expenditure (BE 2026-27: about 26% of total spending and 40% of revenue receipts), ahead of defence, subsidies, grants and pensions.

102.s:
Consider the following statements about Union expenditure (BE 2026-27):
1. Interest payments are about 26% of total spending and 40% of revenue receipts.
2. Revenue expenditure has fallen from 88% of total expenditure (2014-15) to about 77%.
3. Total Union spending is about 16.2% of GDP.
4. Committed expenditure (salaries, pensions, interest) is 65.3% of revenue receipts.
How many of the above statements are correct?
102.x: Three are correct (1, 2, 4). Statement 3 is wrong: total spending of ₹53,47,315 crore is 13.6% of GDP (revenue expenditure alone is 10.5%).

102.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Revenue expenditure is the largest block of the Union Budget.
Reason (R): Interest payments are the largest item of Union revenue expenditure.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
102.x: Both are true: revenue expenditure (about 77% of the total) is bigger than capital expenditure, and interest payments are its largest item. But interest alone (about 26% of spending) does not explain why the whole revenue block is the largest.

102.s:
Match List-I (Where the rupee goes, BE 2026-27) with List-II (Share):
List-I | List-II
a. States' share of taxes | i. 17%
b. Interest | ii. 22%
c. Central Sector Schemes | iii. 11%

102.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?

n: Capital expenditure strengthens long-term productive capacity. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 68-69]
Revenue expenditure does not create assets. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 68-69]
Capital expenditure involves asset creation or acquisition. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 68-69]

102.s:

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
102.x: Both are true and R explains A: the test is whether the government's assets or liabilities change – repayment reduces a liability, so it is capital; capital expenditure also buys, creates, upgrades or extends the life of assets.

102.s:
Consider the following statements:

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
102.x: A is false: the Golden Rule allows borrowing only for asset creation (capital expenditure), not for salaries or pensions. R is true.

n: The source of internal debt is the domestic economy. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 91-92]
External debt may involve foreign currency or foreign-denominated obligations. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 91-92]
The key idea of internal debt is domestic borrowing. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 91-92]
xs: Statements **I and II only** are correct — option **(4)**.
I: correct — internal debt is **raised within the domestic economy**.
II: correct — its key idea is **domestic borrowing**, generally in **domestic currency**.
III: incorrect — **foreign-denominated obligations** belong to **external debt**.
xa: Internal debt creditors: **domestic lenders, institutions or investors**.
Instruments: **G-Secs**, **T-Bills** and others; G-Secs are over **90%** of Central debt.
**Market loans** are a component of internal debt (APPSC-G2 2017).

n: The Consolidated Fund of India is the main government account. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
Government revenues are credited to the Consolidated Fund of India. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
The government is liable to repay or use money from the Public Account of India according to applicable rules. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 88-89]
xa: The **Contingency Fund** is for **urgent and unforeseen expenditure**.
The **State Provident Fund** is part of the **Public Account**.
Public debt is raised against the **Consolidated Fund**; small savings and PF are "other liabilities".

105.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. FRBM amendment incorporating Effective Revenue Deficit
B. Agreement between the RBI and Government relating to ad hoc Treasury Bills
C. Abolition of ad hoc Treasury Bills
D. Introduction of Effective Revenue Deficit in the Union Budget
105.x: The correct sequence is the 1994 agreement, abolition of ad hoc Treasury Bills from 1 April 1997, introduction of ERD in 2011-12, and its incorporation through the 2012 amendment.
105.tq: Fix the dated anchor points first and then place the budget and amendment developments.
xs: Correct order: **B, C, D, A** — option **(1)**.
**B** — RBI-Government agreement **1994**; **C** — ad hoc T-bills abolished from **1 April 1997**.
**D** — ERD introduced in **Union Budget 2011-12**; **A** — written into FRBM by the **2012 amendment**.
xa: Ad hoc T-bills were replaced by **Ways and Means Advances (WMA)**.
After 1997, **budget deficit** stopped being the headline measure.
ERD is a **Rangarajan Committee** concept.

105.x: Fiscal objectives are growth, equity (distributive justice), employment and price stability; price stability completes the list. Reduction of inequalities repeats distributive justice.

105.x: Exchange-rate stabilisation is a classic monetary-policy objective, listed with growth, full employment and price stability; fiscal objectives stress growth, equity, employment and price stability.

progressive taxation combined with regressive expenditure
regressive taxation combined with regressive expenditure
regressive taxation combined with progressive expenditure
105.x: Progressive taxation takes more from higher incomes and progressive expenditure benefits the poor, so together they redistribute income best.

105.s: In the classical range of IS-LM model the
o: Fiscal policy is effective if investment is interest-elastic
Fiscal policy is ineffective even if investment is not completely interest-inelastic

105.x: In the classical range the LM curve is vertical, so extra government spending only raises interest rates and fully crowds out private investment: fiscal policy is ineffective, while monetary policy is fully effective.

105.s:
Assertion (A): Fiscal policy includes taxation, expenditure and public debt.
Reason (R): The fiscal objectives include growth, employment, price stability and equity.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false

105.x: Both are true: fiscal policy is made up of taxation, spending and public debt, and its aims are growth, jobs, price stability and equity. Its aims do not explain what it is made of, so R does not explain A.
n: Fiscal policy includes taxation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
Fiscal policy includes expenditure. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
Fiscal policy includes public debt. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
Fiscal policy objectives include growth. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
Fiscal policy objectives include employment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
Fiscal policy objectives include price stability. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
Fiscal policy objectives include equity. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
**Fiscal policy** includes **taxation**, **expenditure** and **public debt** (A).
Its objectives — **growth, employment, price stability and equity** (R) — are its aims, not what it consists of.
xa: Fiscal policy is made by the **Ministry of Finance**; the **Union Budget** is prepared by **DEA** under **Art. 112**.
⚠ **Directing interest rates** and managing **money supply** belong to **monetary policy**.
**Fiscus** (Latin) = "basket" / public purse.

105.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the fiscal concept involved?

105.tq: Start from the sure conceptual pair and eliminate reversed meanings.

(4) is wrong: public capex attracting private investment is **crowding in**, not crowding out.
xa: **Crowding out**: heavy govt borrowing pushes up **interest rates** → private investment falls.
Related terms: **fiscal drag**, **pump priming**, **fiscal neutrality**.
**Neutral** stance = balanced effect on demand.

3. The Act was enacted on 26 August 2003 and came into force, with its Rules, on 5 July 2004.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the FRBM objectives are inter-generational equity, macro stability, eliminating the revenue deficit, cutting the fiscal deficit, debt management and transparency – the repo rate is fixed by the RBI's monetary policy, not by the FRBM Act. The Bill was introduced in 2000 (FM Yashwant Sinha), enacted 26 August 2003 and in force with the Rules from 5 July 2004.

3. The tax-GDP ratio is a legally binding target under the Act.
4. The RBI was to stay out of primary issues of Government securities from 2006-07.
How many of the above statements are correct?
106.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the tax-GDP ratio is not a legal target; it is one of the four indicators (RD, FD, tax-GDP, total outstanding liabilities) in the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement. The Rules prescribed annual cuts of 0.3% (FD) and 0.5% (RD) of GDP, capped extra guarantees at 0.5% of GDP a year and kept the RBI out of primary G-Sec issues from 2006-07.

106.s: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act does not

106.x:
Official APPSC key: (c), no penal provisions. Strictly (d) is also not done: the Union FRBM Act binds only the Centre, and States have their own Fiscal Responsibility Acts (Ramesh Singh Indian Economy 06 p.18.18).
The FRBM Act prescribes deficit limits and statements to be laid with the Budget but has no penal provisions for missing targets.

106.x: Statement 2 is NOT correct: the committee proposed an independent, advisory Fiscal Council with no binding powers. It recommended RD of 0.8% by 2023 and an escape clause of up to 0.5% of GDP whose triggers include far-reaching structural reforms.

3. It set a fiscal deficit target of 3% of GDP by 31 March 2021.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the 2018 amendment targets debt and the fiscal deficit simultaneously and does away with the revenue deficit (and effective revenue deficit) target. It fixed general government debt 60% / Centre 40% by 31 March 2025 and FD 3% by 31 March 2021.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the escape clause of the amended FRBM Act:
1. National security, war, national calamity and collapse of agriculture are among its grounds.
2. It can be triggered when real output growth falls at least 3 percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters.
3. It allows the fiscal deficit to exceed the target by up to 1% of GDP in a year.
4. When it is invoked, the Government must place a justification and a path back to the target before Parliament.
How many of the above statements are correct?
106.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the permitted deviation is at most 0.5% of GDP a year. The grounds include national security, war, national calamity, agricultural collapse, structural reforms and a sharp output fall (growth 3 percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters) – not a routine tax shortfall – and a justification and path back must be laid before Parliament.

106.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Vijay Kelkar headed the Thirteenth Finance Commission. His 2004 Task Force recommended meeting FRBM targets by tax reform (wider base, comprehensive GST); criticisms of the regime include frequent escape-clause use, deferrals, no penalty and no fiscal council set up yet.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the Union's fiscal consolidation path:
1. The fiscal deficit peaked at 9.2% of GDP in 2020-21.
2. The target set in FY 2021-22 of bringing the fiscal deficit below 4.5% of GDP by 2025-26 was met.
3. The new debt rule of Budget 2026-27 aims to bring Central debt to 40 ± 1% of GDP by 31 March 2031.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the new debt rule targets Central debt of 50 ± 1% of GDP by 31 March 2031 (55.6% in BE 2026-27) – above FRBM's 40%. FD peaked at 9.2% in 2020-21 and the 'below 4.5% by 2025-26' target was met (4.4%); BE 2026-27 is 4.3%.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sixteenth Finance Commission's fiscal recommendations:
1. It recommended a narrower deficit definition that leaves out off-budget borrowing.
2. It recommended a Centre fiscal deficit of 3.5% of GDP by 2030-31 and 3% of GSDP for States.
3. It described State fiscal rules as 'effectively unenforced'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the 16th FC recommended a wider definition of deficit that includes off-budget borrowing. It recommended Centre FD 3.5% by 2030-31 and States 3% of GSDP, and called State fiscal rules 'effectively unenforced'.

107.x: Statement 3 is wrong: dividends and profits are NON-tax revenue (with interest receipts, fees, fines and grants). Revenue receipts create no liability and do not reduce assets; capital receipts – borrowings, small savings, recovery of loans and disinvestment – create a liability or reduce assets.

107.x: Pairs 2 and 3 are wrong: interest payments were NON-plan expenditure (with salaries, pensions, defence, subsidies and public administration), and defence is NON-developmental expenditure. 107.s:
Consider the following statements about deficit measures:
1. Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings.
2. Revenue deficit is revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts.
3. Budget deficit is the excess of total expenditure over revenue receipts only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the budget (budgetary) deficit is total expenditure minus ALL receipts (revenue + capital); it was discontinued from 1996-97. Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − receipts excluding borrowings; primary deficit = FD − interest; revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts.

107.s: Which one of the following is responsible for the preparation and presentation of the Union Budget to the Parliament?
107.x: The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs (Ministry of Finance) is responsible for preparing and presenting the Union Budget; Revenue, Financial Services and Expenditure are not.

107.x: The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs (Ministry of Finance) prepares and presents the Union Budget; the Department of Revenue only handles tax estimates.

107.s: Which one of the following is not a Department in the Ministry of Finance?
107.x: Expenditure, Revenue and Economic Affairs are Departments of the Ministry of Finance; 'Banking Division' is not a Department (it was a division within Financial Services).

107.s: The revenue estimates of the Budget in India are prepared by :
o: The Central Board of Direct Taxes
107.x: Revenue estimates are prepared in the Ministry of Finance – its Department of Revenue, with CBDT and CBIC; CBDT alone, the Cabinet Secretariat or 'commissions' are not the answer.

107.s: All revenues received by the Union Government by way of taxes and other receipts for the conduct of Government business are credited to the
107.x: All revenues, loans raised and loan repayments received by the Union are credited to the Consolidated Fund of India; the Public Account holds provident funds, deposits etc., and the Contingency Fund is a small advance fund.

107.s: Which one of the following is responsible for the preparation of Union Budget?
107.x: The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs (Finance Ministry) prepares the Union Budget.

107.s: Which of the following is not involved in the preparation of budget?
107.x: The Budget is prepared by the Finance Ministry with inputs from ministries (and, then, the Planning Commission); the CAG audits accounts after spending and the FC award feeds the budget, so the CAG is not involved in preparing it.

107.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Appropriation Bill?
107.x: Article 114 covers the Appropriation Bill; 112 is the Annual Financial Statement, 113 the estimates, 115 supplementary grants.
xa: **Art. 116** = **vote on account**, vote of credit, exceptional grants; **Art. 117** = special provisions on financial bills.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the Union Budget:
1. The word 'budget' comes from the French 'bougette' (little bag), and Article 112 of the Constitution uses the word 'budget'.
2. The Department of Economic Affairs also prepares the budgets of States under President's Rule and of Union Territories.
3. The revenue estimates are furnished by the Department of Revenue through the CBDT and the CBIC.
4. As the main instrument of fiscal policy, the Budget performs allocation, redistribution and stabilisation functions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is wrong: 'budget' does come from the French 'bougette' (little bag), but the Constitution does NOT use the word – Article 112 speaks of the 'Annual Financial Statement'. The Budget Division of DEA also prepares budgets of States under President's Rule and UTs; revenue estimates come from the Department of Revenue (CBDT, CBIC); the Budget serves allocation, redistribution and stabilisation.

107.x: Pair 3 is wrong: Article 266(2) provides for the Public Account; the Consolidated Fund of India is under Article 266(1). Art. 115 – supplementary/additional/excess grants; Art. 116 – vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional grants; Art. 267 – Contingency Fund (corpus ₹30,000 crore from FY 2021-22).

Consider the following statements:

Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
107.x: A is false: withdrawals from the Public Account need NO parliamentary appropriation – unlike the Consolidated Fund. R is true: the Public Account (Art. 266(2)) holds money the Government keeps as a banker – provident funds, small savings, deposits.

107.s: Why the Budget presentation date is advanced by Government of India to 1st February?

Reason (R): Presenting it earlier lets the Budget be passed before 31 March, so ministries can spend from the start of the financial year without a vote on account.

o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

107.s: When was gender budgeting initiated in India?
107.x:
Most books and keys: Union Budget 2005-06. Ramesh Singh: gender budgeting started with Union Budget 2006-07 (₹28,737 crore, cells in 32 ministries) (Ramesh Singh Indian Economy 06 p.26).

107.s: Which method of budgeting is concerned with the necessities of future instead of the past?
107.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
107.x: Zero-based budgeting starts every period from zero and judges each item by future needs, not by last year's spending.

107.s: Which of the following is not a necessary component of gender budgeting?
o: Alignment of gender equality policy with the macro-economic policy
Budget outcomes to be assessed with a gender perspective
Better targeting and more efficient utilization of resources
107.x: Gender budgeting is not a separate budget for women; it aligns gender policy with macro policy, assesses outcomes with a gender lens and targets resources better.

107.s: Fresh evaluation of every item of expenditure from the very beginning of each financial year is called as
107.x: Zero-based budgeting is the fresh evaluation of every item of expenditure from zero each period; performance budgeting links spending to work done.

107.s: In which year zero based budget was introduced first time in India?
107.x:
Most books and keys: 1986-87 (Government of India). Strictly: first introduced in the Department of Science and Technology in 1983; Ramesh Singh says in practice since 1997-99 (Ramesh Singh Indian Economy 06 p.25).
The Government of India adopted zero-based budgeting across ministries from 1986-87, the usual exam answer; the Department of Science and Technology had tried it first in 1983.

107.s: A budgeting process which demands each manager to justify his entire budget in detail from beginning is
107.x: Zero-base budgeting requires each manager to justify the entire budget in detail from a zero base every period, not just the increase over last year.

107.s: The concept of Performance Budget has been borrowed from :
107.x: Performance budgeting came from the USA, on the recommendation of the first Hoover Commission (1949).

107.s: In which of the following countries, zero-based budgeting was first adopted?
107.x: Zero-based budgeting was first adopted in the USA (Peter Pyhrr; Jimmy Carter in Georgia, then the US budget).

107.s: What is a budget in which receipts equal expenditure called?
107.x: A balanced budget has receipts equal to expenditure; a surplus budget curbs inflation but may slow growth.
xa: **Zero-based budgeting** — developed by **Peter Pyhrr**; first used in government by **Jimmy Carter**.
**Outcome** and **Gender** budgets date from **2005-06**.
**Performance budgeting** came from the **First Hoover Commission** (USA).

107.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Type of budgeting)
a. Zero-based budgeting
b. Performance budgeting
c. Outcome budgeting
d. Gender budgeting
List-II (Meaning)
i. Links spending to activities and work done
ii. Links outlays to outputs and outcomes
iii. Every item justified afresh from zero each period
iv. Gender-sensitive allocation and assessment of outcomes
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
107.x: ZBB – every item justified afresh from zero, looking to future needs; performance budgeting – spending linked to activities and work done (USA, first Hoover Commission 1949); outcome budgeting – outlays linked to outputs and outcomes (India 2005-06); gender budgeting – gender-sensitive allocation and assessment, not a separate budget for women.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Zero-based budgeting was proposed by Peter Pyhrr.
2. Jimmy Carter first used zero-based budgeting in government, in Georgia.
3. Performance budgeting was first recommended by the second Hoover Commission in the USA.
4. India introduced performance budgeting in the late 1960s on the advice of the Administrative Reforms Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
107.x: Statement 3 is NOT correct: performance budgeting was first recommended by the FIRST Hoover Commission (1949). ZBB was proposed by Peter Pyhrr and first used in government by Jimmy Carter (Georgia, 1973 budget); India adopted performance budgeting in the late 1960s on the ARC's advice.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gender Budget Statement:
1. It is Statement 13 of the Union Budget documents.
2. Part B covers schemes in which 30-99% of the allocation is for women.
3. Part C covers schemes in which 100% of the allocation is for women.
4. In 2026-27 it was about ₹5.01 lakh crore, or 9.37% of the total Budget.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 3 is wrong: Part A covers schemes with 100% allocation for women; Part C covers those below 30%. The Gender Budget Statement is Statement 13; Part B is 30-99%; in 2026-27 it reached ₹5.01 lakh crore (9.37%), the highest ever.

107.s: What happens to demands for grants when the Guillotine procedure is applied in Parliament?
o: They are sent back to the ministry for revision
They are put to vote without further discussion
They are debated in detail before voting
107.src: APPSC AEE (Civil), AMVI, Agriculture Officer and Other Posts
107.x: Under the guillotine the Speaker puts all outstanding demands to vote on the last allotted day, whether discussed or not; they are not sent back, debated or rejected.

107.s: The provision which empowers Lok Sabha to make any grant in advance for part of a financial year pending completion of budgetary process is called?
107.x: Article 116 lets the Lok Sabha make a grant in advance for part of the year pending the budget – the vote on account; a vote of credit is for unexpected demands.

107.s: Which one of the following motions has contextual relationship with the Union Budget :
107.x: Cut motions are moved during voting on the Demands for Grants, so they relate to the Budget; censure, call-attention and adjournment motions are not budget instruments.

107.s: With respect to the procedure of Budget in the Parliament, "the amount of demand be reduced to Rs. 1" is called :
107.x: A motion that 'the amount of the demand be reduced to ₹1' is the policy cut (disapproval of policy); the economy cut reduces by a specified amount and the token cut by ₹100.

107.s: The Indian Parliament exercises control on the audit of the Budget through its :
107.x: Parliament controls the audit of the Budget through the Public Accounts Committee, which examines the CAG's reports; the Estimates Committee looks at estimates, not audit.

107.s:
What is the difference between ‘Vote on Account’ and ‘Interim Budget’?

I. The provision of a ‘Vote on Account’ is used by a regular Government, while an ‘Interim Budget’ is a provision used by a caretaker Government.

II. A ‘Vote on Account’ only deals with the expenditure in Government’s budget, while an ‘Interim Budget’ includes both expenditure and receipts.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
107.x: A vote on account covers only expenditure, while an interim budget is a full statement of receipts and expenditure, so II is correct; I is wrong because both are used by the government in an election year, not as a caretaker-only device.

107.s: In the Indian Parliamentary System, ‘Vote on Account’ is valid for how many months (except the year of elections)?
107.x: A vote on account is generally granted for two months (one-sixth of the estimate); only in election years is it taken for 3-5 months.

107.s:
Arrange the following stages of the Union Budget process in the correct chronological order:
A. Voting on Demands for Grants
B. Presentation of the Budget
C. Finance Bill
D. General discussion
107.x: The sequence is presentation, general discussion, voting on Demands for Grants and then the Finance Bill, with the Appropriation Bill preceding the Finance Bill.
107.tq: Fix the first and last stages, then place discussion and voting between them.
xs: Order: **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)**.
**Presentation** → **general discussion** → **DRSC scrutiny** → **voting on demands** → **Appropriation Bill** → **Finance Bill**.
The **Finance Bill** is the **last** stage, after the Appropriation Bill.
xa: General discussion: both Houses, **3-4 days**; no cut motions.
Voting on demands (**Art. 113**): **only Lok Sabha**.
Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days**.

107.s: What does the Halwa ceremony in the Union Budget process mark?
107.x: The Halwa ceremony marks the printing of the Budget documents; the Budget circular is issued earlier, in September.
xa: The DEA also prepares budgets of **States under President's Rule** and **UTs**.
Revenue estimates come from **CBDT/CBIC** (Department of Revenue).

107.s: In which month is the Budget circular issued to begin preparation of the Union Budget?
107.x: The Budget circular is issued in September; the Halwa ceremony later marks printing of the documents.

List-I (Term)
a. Policy cut
b. Economy cut
c. Token cut
d. Guillotine
List-II (Meaning)
i. Demand reduced to ₹1 – disapproval of the policy
ii. Demand reduced by a specified amount

iv. Demand reduced by ₹100 – a specific grievance

107.x: Policy cut – demand reduced to ₹1; economy cut – reduced by a specified amount; token cut – reduced by ₹100 to air a specific grievance; guillotine – on the last day the Speaker puts all outstanding demands to vote without further discussion.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the passage of the Budget:
1. Only the Lok Sabha votes on the Demands for Grants.
2. Cut motions are moved at the stage of general discussion on the Budget.
3. The Finance Bill, which gives effect to the tax proposals, must be enacted within 75 days under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 2 is wrong: no cut motion is moved in the general discussion; cut motions are moved at the stage of voting on Demands for Grants, which only the Lok Sabha votes on. The Finance Bill (a Money Bill) must be enacted within 75 days under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931.

107.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A vote on account is provided for under Article 115 of the Constitution.
2. In an election year a vote on account may cover 3-5 months instead of the normal two.
3. An interim budget is a full statement of receipts and expenditure presented by the government in an election year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is wrong: a vote on account is under Article 116 (Article 115 deals with supplementary, additional and excess grants). It normally covers two months (one-sixth), 3-5 months in election years; an interim budget is a full statement of receipts and expenditure.
